served_regression_found.candidate49_vs_1107: 42 of 116 short-extent sweep cells slower beyond the interval (two warmed boots, json/r1w-short-sweep-boot*.json): 520..4,096-entry extents with 256..1,024 rows, 29 of the 30 sampled causal 1,024-row chunks below position 8,192 (the other within the interval; all 32 chunks at positions 8,192..32,767 are gains), and the reindex selector at 4,096 candidates x 256 rows
served_regression_found.cause: The one-pass 16,384-entry kernel keeps the compile-time compaction ownership per = 32 for a partly filled row: with n live keys only n/32 threads work, each reading 32 keys twice in series (a 2,048-entry row leaves 448 of 512 threads idle), where 1107's 4,096-entry segment reads 8 per thread; and its 32 KiB key array holds 2 CTAs/SM against 1107's 3 (512 threads, about 23 KiB), so at many rows the longer per-CTA compaction is exposed

change.summary: In _select_macros' compact (used by every segment and merge kernel): with an active count n, each thread owns ceil(n / 512) consecutive keys instead of per, so a partial segment or merge group is spread over all threads; and one block scan of packed (ties << 16 | above) counts replaces the two scans, using that the ties kept before a thread equal min(ties needed, ties before it). The packed scan is compiled only where per * threads < 32768. Segment sizes, routes, merge fan-in and gather paths are unchanged.
change.exactness_argument: Ownership stays contiguous and in thread order, so selected positions are written in ascending entry order with ties at the threshold taken lowest-first, as before; min(need, ties before) is the running sum of the per-thread tie quotas max(min(need - ties_before, ties), 0) that the second scan computed

change.how_chosen: Two variants were timed against 1107 and candidate-49 on the losing regime (raw/diag-variants-run1.txt, clean): ownership spread alone (scripts/variants/indexer_dynper.diff) left N=4096 x 1024 rows at 76.99 us against 1107's 79.03 (a tie); with the single packed scan (indexer_dynper1scan.diff, the change submitted) 68.78

reason: The reported cell is not on any serving path: serving never builds the standalone 1M-wide k=512 selector (Layer 20 uses #999's gather select, the other layers 524288- or 16384-wide plans), and the correction makes that cell a gain as well (35.79/35.37 us against 38.92/39.17). But enumerating every served shape found a served shape #999's grid does not time: the dense layers' 16,384-entry short-prefill selector, where candidate-49 was slower than 1107 beyond the interval in 42 of 116 cells (up to 22%; 29 of 30 sampled 1,024-row chunks below position 8,192). Spreading compaction over every thread and computing the tie quota with one packed scan fixes it: on two clean warmed boots the corrected #999 is faster than 1107 beyond the interval in 210 of 210 PR-bench cells, 148 of 148 served-gap cells and 116 of 116 sweep cells, bit-exact everywhere, and in the same process it is equal to or faster than candidate-49 on the full-extent served selectors except two cells slower by 0.2 us and 0.05 us.
